question: If \(F(n)\) is a function such that \(F(1)=F(2)=F(3)=1,\) and such that \[ F(n+1)=\frac{F(n)F(n-1)+1}{F(n-2)} \] for \(n\ge3,\) then \(F(6)\) is equal to:
solution:
To find \(F(6)\), first calculate the earlier values it needs. Substituting \(n=3,4,5\) in order gives
\[
F(4)=\frac{F(3)F(2)+1}{F(1)}
=\frac{1\cdot1+1}{1}=2,
\]
\[
F(5)=\frac{F(4)F(3)+1}{F(2)}
=\frac{2\cdot1+1}{1}=3,
\]
and
\[
F(6)=\frac{F(5)F(4)+1}{F(3)}
=\frac{3\cdot2+1}{1}=7.
\]
All denominators used are the given initial values \(1\), so each division is valid. Therefore \(F(6)=7\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
